correctness.rationale: A complete, quantified structural proof enumerates all successful initial states. For q<r the embedded K_r obstructs any completion. At q=r the hub cannot be forced until each blade has >=r-2 seeds, and hub-seeded and hub-unseeded cases yield respectively zH_r(z)^m and H_r(z)^m-(r-1)z^(m(r-2)) per completed color assignment. For q>r every leaf has degree r-1<q-1, so all leaves are seeds and the hub can be forced iff the q-1 non-hub colors are all present, giving exact inclusion-exclusion. All thresholds and multiplicities follow, as does the weighted probability transform. An independently coded adjacency-based exhaustive checker enumerated 489,479 complete seed states across 12 cases, confirming each coefficient; its finite checks are supplementary to the proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives all coefficients, and thus all exact forcing probabilities and successful seed counts, in a natural infinite two-parameter family for every named palette q. It proves a substantive structural phase transition: one extra color beyond the chromatic palette forbids all leaf-forcing events and increases the minimum initial domain by exactly m. This sharp rigidity and full distribution are motivated by propagation on cut-vertex clique blocks, rather than an arbitrary finite instance.
